newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - BME/Reuters German July PMI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - BME/Reuters German July PMI.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments from economists on the July Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) which fell to a seasonally-adjusted 55.32 from 56.83 in June.
Volker Nitsch, Economist at Bankgesellschaft Berlin:

"The number itself is not surprising, it is in line with our expectations. The economic upturn is still going on - it's still on track. But the upturn is still not as strong as it should be at this stage of the cycle."

DAVID BRICKMAN, EUROPEAN ECONOMIST AT YAMAICHI: "The evidence here is that we have a clear differential between the two sectors of the economy. The export sector is quite clearly booming led on by the weakness of the deutschemark but the domestic sector remains chronically weak and as a result we have a worsening sector once again in the labour market.
"It has to raise questions about whether the Bundesbank could seriously consider raising interest rates in such an environment unless the deutschemark weakens significantly further from here."
RALPH SUEPPEL, HEAD OF ECONOMIC RESEARCH, JP MORGAN IN FRANKFURT:

"For the Bundesbank it is difficult to raise rates at this point in time because prices are stable in Germany. I think from the growth side...the recovery is mainly export-led, that's not surprising...against the backdrop of the strong of the weak currency... There are signs that exports are starting to spill over into better domestic demand."
